name: NJ-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+14 district with a four-decade incumbent in Chris Smith
Rachel Peace badly outraised, with about $5,000 cash on hand versus $488,000

model.rationale: The district's fourteen-point Republican lean, Smith's long incumbency, and a lopsided money gap overwhelm a modestly favorable national environment for Democrats, and markets and fundamentals agree the seat is not in play.
model.watch: Any significant shift in the national environment toward Democrats or an unexpected development in Smith's candidacy would be needed to bring this into range.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
New Jersey's 4th District leans heavily Republican by roughly fourteen points, and Chris Smith has held the seat since 1981, making him one of the longest-serving members of the House. He enters the general election with about $488,000 in cash on hand after raising roughly $592,000. His Democratic challenger, Rachel Peace, has raised about $34,000 with just over $5,000 available, and no outside spending has been reported on either side.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, and prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point the same way: the district's lean, Smith's incumbency advantage, and the large financial gap all favor the Republican. The national environment offers Democrats some benefit, but it is unlikely to overcome the structural advantages Smith holds in this district, leaving the race rated Safe Republican.
